messages:
Sara: Heads-up — our Monday product launch now overlaps an EoQ promo and there's a provider egress maintenance notice for eu-west (02:00-06:00 UTC). They expect ~=30% cross-region bandwidth reduction. Simulation (no throttles) shows peak ~1.1M tokens/sec and ~650 GPU-hours across 6h. We need an operational plan: rate-shaping waves, pre-warm, and fallbacks. cc @Mike @Jonathan :eyes:
Mike: can you drop the sim output? is that with prefix caching + batching?
Sara: sim attached (summarized): peak RPS 14k, avg latency 280ms without shaping; with prefix cache and 8x batching latency target ~120-150ms. GPU-hour calc assumes p3x16 equiv and baseline model (unquantized).
Jonathan: big flag: egress limit means cross-region fallback will saturate. If eu-west can't call eu-central fast enough, we'll see queueing at the gateway. Recommend local-rate-shaping per-region and a multi-wave ramp.
Ashley: +1 on waves. Proposed wave plan: 0-30m 10% traffic, 30-90m 40%, 90-240m 70%, keep 70% for remainder. Each wave should have a canary group (5% users) with full observability.
Kevin: cost check: with Ashley's ramp we'd cut estimated GPU-hours from ~650 to ~430 (rough calc). But reserved capacity requests for extra GPUs need 72h lead. Do we have capacity headroom in prod pools?
Sara: current pool headroom: ~120 GPUs free in eu-west and 60 in us-west. If we lock 50 GPUs for dedicated run, we still need autoscale policy tweak.
Mike: ops plan ideas: 1) API gateway rate shaping by customer tier + region; 2) prefer local quantized model variant when latency starts climbing; 3) prewarm KV caches and keep warm dedicated nodes for fast attach.
Jonathan: for (2) how much perf delta? Quantized model gives ~1.8x throughput increase but ~2-3% quality drift. We can route low-risk classes to quantized during waves. Need QA signoff on acceptable routes.
Ashley: we should prepare a hot-failover policy: if regional egress >25% degraded, route to same-region quantized pool and reduce non-critical batch sizes. Also reduce streaming chunk size from 64->32 tokens to lower tail latency.
Sara: action items: Mike = rate-shaping config + deploy test, Jonathan = quantized routing matrix and QA checklist, Kevin = capacity lock request w/ procurement, Ashley = canary dashboard + SLO alarms. I'll coordinate runbook updates.
Mike: I'll prototype gateway config. Example rule (WIP):
```
# gateway rate rule (pseudo)
- region: eu-west
  tier: free
  rate: 5rps
- region: eu-west
  tier: paid
  rate: 50rps
- ramp: wave_percent -> multiply_token_budget
```
I'll also add token-bucket fallback so we don't cause 500s.
infra-bot: deploy-candidate: canary-traffic 5% to eu-west applied by deploy-bot at 1849123500
Ashley: infra-bot noted. We'll watch error-rate, p95 lat, token cost, and queue length. Dashboard urls: https://console.redwood/boards/launch-wave (private)
Kevin: procurement asked for justification; I've put a note: "temporary reserved capacity for launch to maintain latency SLOs under provider network maintenance". Need final GPU count by EOD so procurement can finish.
Sara: final numbers proposed: lock 50 GPUs in eu-west for 12h window, shape waves as Ashley suggested, quantized fallback for non-critical routes, canary 5% -> 20% ramp. If everyone ok I'll file the change and schedule a dry-run tonight at 23:30 UTC.
Mike: ok from me. I'll push a draft config to infra-playbooks and run the dry-run logs.
Jonathan: QA will run prompt-sample regression on the quantized path during dry-run.
Ashley: I'll own alerts and runbook. I'll make a short checklist and set Slack pings for metrics > threshold. :thumbsup:
Sara: thanks team. quick note — keep customer-facing rate limits conservative to avoid cascades. ping me if you hit blockers.
Kevin: noting cost cutoff: prefer quantized if cost > $X/hr per 10k tokens threshold (we'll set threshold tomorrow).
Mike: posted draft: https://git.redwood/infra/rate-shaping/launch-wave (WIP)
infra-bot: canary-dryrun completed at 1849123605, status: ok (no 5xx spike).
Sara: great — looks like dry-run went well. We'll reconvene 02:30 UTC for launch watch.
